title: Bypassed Aggregate Root (Direct Child Modification)
pattern: An aggregate's child entities are exposed as public collections, allowing clients to add, remove, or modify children without navigating through the Aggregate Root's API.
why_bad: It breaks the aggregate boundary. The parent `Order` can no longer enforce overall invariants (such as maximum order amounts or duplicate checks) because clients can mutate the child collection directly, leading to data corruption.
detection: A collection of entities inside a struct is marked public, or exposed via public getters returning mutable references, allowing arbitrary external mutations.
counterexample: Simple data structures with no business invariants or validation rules where raw collections are acceptable.
source: *Eric Evans - Domain-Driven Design, Chapter 6 (Managing the Life Cycle of a Domain Object), Section "AGGREGATES"*
